Device fingerprint: establish its necessity and proportionality for this scoring purpose; exclude or reduce it if not necessary and set a justified retention period.

Document an Article 6 legal basis for scoring and for sharing scores with the vendor; the transfer mechanism does not itself establish a lawful processing purpose.

Creditworthiness assessment is high-risk AI, not the financial-fraud detection exception. Before deployment, complete the required fundamental-rights impact assessment and meet deployer obligations, including use according to instructions, monitoring, and log retention.

DPO review is required before build because the feature involves automated decision-making. This activity has no matching register entry; only DPO approval can make this assessment an organisational record.
The US vendor transfer is covered by the organisation’s stated Data Privacy Framework certification fact; record this transfer in the transfer log and verify the certification remains applicable.

Justify the use of transaction history, device fingerprint, and browsing behaviour individually; document the legal bases, purposes, minimisation, and retention.

assessment.summary: Creditworthiness scoring is a high-risk AI use under AI Act Annex III point 5(b). Complete a DPIA before processing: this is systematic, extensive profiling informing decisions with significant effects. As deployer of an Annex III point 5(b) system, also complete a fundamental-rights impact assessment before deployment.

The model evaluates creditworthiness, so it is high-risk AI. Fine-tuning and putting it under your brand may make the company a provider; determine whether the modification is substantial and confirm the contractual allocation. Tell customers that the high-risk AI system is used in decisions about them; telling them only the outcome is not enough. Provide clear, meaningful explanations of the system’s role and main decision elements to affected people who qualify for the explanation right.

A credit officer approves or changes each proposed limit before application, so the described decision is not solely automated, provided the officer genuinely reviews the recommendation and can independently reject or override it.

Set and justify retention periods for the ID-document scan and yes/no result; retain no more than needed and consider whether the full scan can be avoided or reduced.

If a failed match automatically prevents account opening or otherwise significantly affects the applicant, provide applicable human intervention and a way to contest the outcome; the video-call option should allow meaningful review.
Tell customers before collection about purposes, legal bases, retention, whether biometric verification is optional, and the consequences of choosing video call or not providing data.
Deleting face templates immediately after matching limits their retention, as described. Ensure deletion includes temporary copies and vendor-held copies.
As described, one-to-one verification solely to confirm the applicant’s claimed identity for access to the account service is excluded from the AI Act’s high-risk biometric category.

statements.reason: Art. 17(3) says paragraphs 1 and 2 do not apply to the extent processing is necessary for the listed purposes, and Art. 17(1) requires erasure without undue delay where a ground applies. Read together, data necessary under an exception may be retained while the remainder is erased.
